# 2026 Winners

### Best Statistical Analysis

<!-- ::: {.column-margin} -->
<!-- ![](images/2025/best_stat.jpeg) -->
<!-- ::: -->

["From Patterns to Prevention: How Social Determinants Shape Type 2 Diabetes Care Pathways"](/presentations/CarolinaCorrelations2026.pdf) by Eric Hu, Ruitong Liu, Mia Zhou, and Gloria Yang.

*Their customer risk model particularly stood out to the judges as providing a potential for large eﬀiciency improvement and overall improved customer outcomes.*

### Best Insight

<!-- ::: {.column-margin} -->
<!-- ![](images/2025/best_insight.jpeg) -->
<!-- ::: -->

["Financial Friction: Markov Analysis of Patient Journeys"](/presentations/Regressors2026.pdf) by Kat Craig and Sam Adamczeski.

*Judges were impressed by actionable insights that could help improve customer outcomes for those under financial stress. Their insights were based on specific real life examples.*
 

### Best Visualizations

<!-- ::: {.column-margin} -->
<!-- ![](images/2025/best_viz.jpeg) -->
<!-- ::: -->

["Tracing the Last Mile"](/presentations/WeNeedACoolName2026.pdf) by Jovid Jumaev, Long Nguyen, Pratik Shrestha, and Tram Le.

*Judges were impressed by their Sankey plot that detailed the customer journey for sepsis patients, noting this was the best visualization for a customer's journey they saw and helped to convey their overall story about quick diagnosis.*


### Best Use of Outside Data

<!-- ::: {.column-margin} -->
<!-- ![](images/2025/best_data.jpeg) -->
<!-- ::: -->

["Can income predict the rate of chronic disease per county?"](/presentations/UpperCase2026.pdf) by Lucy Liu, Kaya Li, Sathvika Kommera, and Liam Kiley.

*Judges were impressed by this group's use of income data from the census which helped them to analyze how economic situation affected customers.*

<!-- [**Recruitment, distribution and questions**](/presentations/NEON-presentation.pdf) by Sophie Guo, Carrie Hang, Hanoc Codjie, Lipsa Tripathy & Alejandra Camargo. -->

### Judges' Pick

<!-- ::: {.column-margin} -->
<!-- ![](images/2025/judge_pick.jpeg) -->
<!-- ::: -->

*Project recognized by the judges for outstanding achievement outside of the core award categories.*

["The Sepsis Burden: Geographic and Social Disparities represented in Stormont Vail Health"](/presentations/DataDevils2026.pdf) by Tien Thai, Claire Peng, Kaixiang Loke, and Lola Liu.
*Judges were impressed by insights surrounding Sepsis cases and their prevalence being related to socio-economic status as seen by interpretation of the random-forest model.*

### Honorable mention

["Healthcare Utilization & Social Determinants: Trends in ED Use, Admissions, & Length of Stay"](/presentationsd/appleSeers2026.pdf) by Hyunjin Lee, Liane Ma, Cooper Ruffing, and Amy Xu. 

*Judges appreciated actionable insights based on regressions that tied length of stay and repeat visits to socioeconomic factors and barriers to health care providers.*
